title: terraform: private deployment modules - GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking, and state layout
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Added Terraform modules for Private deployments: GPU node pools (GKE/GCP and EKS/AWS), consolidated IAM role modules with least-privilege defaults, VPC/subnet layout improvements, and a predictable remote state layout with migration helper scripts.
description: Motivation: Prepare the Terraform surface for Private deployments that require GPU node pools, constrained IAM roles, robust networking, and a repeatable remote state layout. This PR introduces modular Terraform constructs so Dedicated/Private installers can compose cloud resources consistently across clouds. Summary of changes: - New modules/gpu_node_pool: encapsulates GPU node pool creation for GKE and EKS, exposes tuning knobs (instance_type, taints/tolerations, autoscaling, gpu_count_per_node, image/boot_disk) and optional node pool autoscaler integration. - New modules/iam/minimum_privilege: consolidated role and policy attachments for private runtime components (controller, installer, metrics exporter) with documentation of required permissions and mapping to service accounts. - Networking adjustments in modules/network: deterministic subnet CIDR allocation, optional private cluster flags, and explicit NAT/gateway configuration for on-prem edge cases. - Remote state layout and migration: redesigned state key layout (env/region/stack) and migration helper scripts to move legacy state blobs to the new layout; included example backfill plan. - Integration: root terraform entrypoints for examples/private-gcp and examples/private-aws that compose the modules and validate outputs. - Docs: updated README and examples, added upgrade notes and a runbook for migrating remote state. Commits (high-level): 1) initial gpu_node_pool module scaffold and tests; 2) IAM module with policies and example mappings; 3) network CIDR allocator and private-cluster flags; 4) remote state layout change + migration helpers; 5) integration example + docs + minor fixes. Files changed (high-level): modules/gpu_node_pool/* (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, tests), modules/iam/* (policies.tf, roles.tf, variables.tf, docs), modules/network/* (cidr_allocator.tf, nat.tf, variables.tf), examples/private-gcp/main.tf, examples/private-aws/main.tf, scripts/state-migrate.py, README.md, docs/upgrade.md. Testing and CI: unit tests for TF modules (terratest) for GKE/EKS examples, linter checks (tflint, tfsec), and CI runs passed after addressing IAM policy formatting in follow-up commit. Review thread summary: - Evan requested tighter defaults for autoscaling thresholds and a clearer variable naming scheme; addressed by renaming min_node_count -> node_min and max_node_count -> node_max, and setting safer defaults. - Priya flagged a potential excessive IAM permission (s3:PutObject in cross-account path); reduced policy to a scoped PutObject and added examples for cross-account delegation. - Liam validated the remote state migration path and requested an explicit dry-run mode in scripts; added --dry-run and verbose flags. Follow-ups and operational notes: - Migration: state-migrate.py must be run from a CI runner with the maintainer key and tested in staging first; instructions included in docs/upgrade.md. - Rollback: added a documented rollback path that reverts to legacy state layout if migration fails; requires manual intervention and support on a case-by-case basis. - Compatibility: examples include a compatibility layer for clusters that do not support GPU instance types (falls back to empty node pool and a warning). Changelog: This PR changes Terraform state layout and introduces new resources; while not a code-breaking API change, operators should follow the upgrade runbook before applying to production. Related: ENG-1428 (private deploy infra), ENG-1462 (gpu autoscale profiles), SUP-912 (customer request for GPU private deployment). Checklist: - [x] Module scaffolds and unit tests - [x] IAM least-privilege review - [x] Network CIDR allocator validated - [x] Remote state migration helper added - [x] Docs and upgrade notes updated Merge: Squash-merged after reviewers approved and CI green.
notes: Hotfix guidance: If operator sees 'state backend path not found' errors after migration, run scripts/state-migrate.py --rollback to restore legacy keys, then open SUP ticket referencing SUP-912.
